reports.title: Annual Consolidated Balance Sheet of the Eurosystem
reports.description: The consolidated year-end balance sheet of the Eurosystem (the ECB and the euro area national central banks), with intra-Eurosystem claims and liabilities netted out. Governed by Annex VII to Guideline (EU) 2024/2941 of the European Central Bank (ECB/2024/31): 'the consolidated annual balance sheet of the Eurosystem' (Article 26(3)(c)). ECB's own landing page lists one dated entry per year, unbroken, from 1999 to 2025.
reports.cadence_note: 27 consecutive years of linked publication (1999-2025) confirmed directly on the ECB's own landing page, each dated in February for the preceding year-end -- e.g. '26 February 2026 -- Consolidated balance sheet of the Eurosystem as at 31 December 2025'.

reports.title: Weekly Financial Statement of the Eurosystem
reports.description: The consolidated weekly financial statement of the Eurosystem, published under Annexes V and VI to Guideline (EU) 2024/2941 (ECB/2024/31): 'the published consolidated weekly financial statement of the Eurosystem after quarter end' and '... during the quarter' (Article 26(3)(a)-(b)). ECB's own landing page: 'The weekly financial statements of the Eurosystem are published on a Tuesday, and they relate to the preceding Friday.'
reports.cadence_note: Stated directly by the ECB: published every Tuesday, relating to the preceding Friday, except the first statement of each quarter, which 'will normally be a Wednesday (instead of Tuesday) in order to allow more time to complete the quarterly revaluation of assets and liabilities'. The fastest-cadence node in the EU branch, faster than eurostat-hicp's monthly cadence.

reports.title: ESS-ESCB Quality Assessment Report on Statistics Underlying the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure
reports.publisher: European Statistical System (ESS) and European System of Central Banks (ESCB)
reports.description: A joint annual quality assessment of the statistics underlying the EU's Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure (MIP) scoreboard and auxiliary indicators, produced jointly by Eurostat/the national statistical institutes (ESS) and the ECB/national central banks (ESCB). The report's own cover, 26 June 2026 edition: 'This 12th joint annual quality report presents a transparent description and assessment of the quality of the statistics underlying the MIP indicators.' Legal/institutional basis: a Memorandum of Understanding between Eurostat and the ECB DG Statistics (November 2016), and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2180, which 'specifies the detailed arrangements and content for the quality reports pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/1700.'
reports.cadence_note: Cadence rests on the report's own stated edition count -- 'This 12th joint annual quality report' -- rather than a counted publication list or a metadata cadence statement, the first EU node in this corpus evidenced this way.

reports.title: Joint ECB-Eurostat Annual Report on the Consistency of National Accounts and Balance of Payments (Quarterly Financial and Non-Financial Accounts)
reports.publisher: European Central Bank and Eurostat, jointly, presented to the CMFB
reports.description: A joint ECB-Eurostat report measuring the consistency between national accounts and balance-of-payments data on quarterly financial and non-financial accounts, presented annually to the Committee on Monetary, Financial and Balance of Payments Statistics (CMFB). CMFB's own page: 'this comparison has been carried out on a regular basis. Since January 2022 a single annual report covers both the financial accounts and the non-financial accounts.' The 2026 edition covers data through Q2 2025.
reports.cadence_note: CMFB's own page, live-verified 2026-08-09: 'a single annual report'.

dependencies.basis: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 6). The June 2026 MIP quality report was fetched directly and re-read specifically for this question; the sentence already quoted in this file's own _dropped entry turns out to be the MIP report's own text, not a third source, and the edge it supports was simply never minted. Full paragraph, Executive summary: 'Moreover, additional efforts are also needed to address the ongoing inconsistencies between BOP/IIP and the "Rest of the World" (ROW) account. Eurostat and the ECB regularly present joint reports on the consistency of the two datasets to the CMFB. The most recent joint ECB-Eurostat "BOP-NA ROW consistency report" was presented to the CMFB plenary in January 2026 and published on the CMFB website in February 2026. This report highlights cross-cutting and transversal issues where efforts need to continue to reduce inconsistencies, with the aim of further enhancing the quality and international comparability of macroeconomic statistics.' Typed `cites` rather than `uses_data_from`: the MIP report names and characterises the other report's findings in its executive-summary discussion of BOP/IIP-NA issues, but does not state that it recalculates or incorporates the other report's data into its own MIP indicators. Checked the opposite direction too, per Research.1.md §3 (report conflicts, don't resolve them one-sided): the BOP-NA consistency report's own CMFB page names the MIP framework only in passing ('In the context of the Macroeconomics Imbalance Procedure (MIP), quality assurance framework issues related to the consistency of the two statistics are addressed as needed') and does not cite the MIP quality report itself. The relationship is one-directional: MIP report cites BOP-NA report, not the reverse.

The footnote is Annex I, footnote (1), attached specifically to row 5 of Annex I's table ('Financial statements for the Eurosystem'): 'Monthly and quarterly financial information of the Eurosystem' -- Internal/published status 'Published and internal', Source of legal requirement 'Statistical regulations, according to which MFIs have to deliver data' (i.e. the same Regulation ECB/2021/2 / Guideline ECB/2021/11 already cited as ecb-mfi-balance-sheet-items's own legal basis). It is NOT attached to row 3 (Consolidated weekly financial statement, 'Article 15.2 of the Statute of the ESCB' -- ecb-eurosystem-weekly-financial-statement) or row 6 (Consolidated annual balance sheet, 'Article 26.3' -- ecb-eurosystem-annual-balance-sheet). The footnote describes the Eurosystem central banks' own dual role as MFI statistical reporters (row 5, governed by the BSI regulations themselves) feeding the published BSI aggregate -- not a dependency of BSI on either of this slice's two accounting-framework nodes. Minting the edge to either existing node would have been a wrong-target error; not minted. Row 5 itself is not proposed as a fifth node -- its 'source of legal requirement' column names the same instruments already governing ecb-mfi-balance-sheet-items, so a separate node would likely duplicate it rather than add a distinct publication. Row 4 ('Disaggregated monthly financial statement of the Eurosystem', status Published, purpose stated as central-bank-level transparency) was noticed in passing and is a genuinely distinct, uninvestigated lead -- not chased this pass.
